# SOP-P2-L4-01 Line startup - Heat Treat line
Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P2, line P2-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L4-RR01, EQ-P2-L4-HT02, EQ-P2-L4-HP03  
Related: ECN-2026-045, SB-1007, SOP-P2-L4-02

Purpose
1. Establish the controlled startup procedure for the Heat Treat line at P2-L4 to ensure safe, repeatable preparation of equipment prior to production, preserve product metallurgical requirements, and document readiness for operations.

Scope
2. Applies to operators, maintenance technicians, and shift leads responsible for EQ-P2-L4-RR01, EQ-P2-L4-HT02, and EQ-P2-L4-HP03 during initial daily startup, post-maintenance returns, and changeover into Heat Treat mode. See SOP-P2-L4-02 for shutdown and changeover steps.

Preconditions
3. Equipment maintenance status must be confirmed in the maintenance log and match the workpack. Confirm there are no outstanding hold tags on EQ-P2-L4-RR01, EQ-P2-L4-HT02, or EQ-P2-L4-HP03. Review ECN-2026-045 for recent engineering changes that affect startup sequence. Confirm utilities are available and stable per plant control room communication. Verify required lubricants and consumables are staged per SB-1007.

Personal protective equipment (PPE)
4. Required PPE for startup:
   - Safety glasses with side shields.
   - Heat-resistant glove set per plant PPE matrix.
   - Steel-toe footwear.
   - Hearing protection (insert provided by plant).
   - Flame-retardant jacket as required when in proximity to furnaces.

Lubricants and consumables
5. Confirm lubricant stock and application points:
   - The lubricant part number for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P2-L4-HP03) is CFW-LUB-450.
   - The lubricant part number for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L4-RR01) is CFW-LUB-723.
   Apply only specified lubricants to their intended reservoirs and tag the return on the MRO ticket.

Background and rationale
6. The Heat Treat line contains sequential mechanical and thermal stages; mechanical alignment and lubrication affect metallurgical outcomes downstream. Proper startup reduces risk of equipment damage, scrap, and safety incidents. This SOP aligns with engineering change ECN-2026-045 and lubrication guidance in SB-1007.

Startup steps (numbered sequence)
7. Step 1 — Pre-start visual inspection
   - Walk the line and inspect EQ-P2-L4-RR01, EQ-P2-L4-HT02, and EQ-P2-L4-HP03 for physical damage, loose guarding, leaks, or foreign objects.
   - Verify furnace doors and safety interlocks are not bypassed and are in the closed/tested position.
   - Record observations in the Startup Checklist.

8. Step 2 — Verify documentation and permits
   - Confirm the machine log and permit to operate are present and signed. Cross-reference recent entries against ECN-2026-045 for any procedure changes.
   - Ensure any outstanding work orders are cleared or approved for operations.

9. Step 3 — Lubrication verification
   - Verify reservoir levels and condition against manufacturer sight gauges and the lubrication schedule in SB-1007.
   - Replenish only with the specified lubricants: CFW-LUB-450 for EQ-P2-L4-HP03 and CFW-LUB-723 for EQ-P2-L4-RR01. Document lot number and MRO ticket number in the equipment log.

10. Step 4 — Control system and interlock checks
    - Put the line control in the local test mode. Verify that E-stop circuits, door interlocks, and furnace safety interlocks register correctly on the HMI without disabling permissive logic.
    - If any interlock fails, stop and call maintenance. Create a work request and reference ECN-2026-045 if function was modified.

11. Step 5 — Power-up sequence
    - Energize mechanical drives and actuators following the control system prompts. Allow control PLCs and HMIs to complete their diagnostics.
    - Observe for abnormal noises, vibration, or alarm conditions. Log anomalies and halt further startup until cleared.

12. Step 6 — Dry run and alignment
    - Jog conveyors and feed mechanisms at low speed to confirm mechanical alignment and smooth travel of tooling. Verify references and zero positions shown on the HMI match the mechanical position.
    - If misalignment is observed, stop and perform corrective maintenance with lockout/tagout per SB-1007.

13. Step 7 — Heat-up procedure
    - Follow the heat-up steps defined in the furnace operating section of SOP-P2-L4-02 and record the sequence in the furnace log. Confirm preheat permissives and that furnace chamber atmosphere controls are active.

14. Step 8 — Trial part run
    - Run a controlled trial of production parts through EQ-P2-L4-RR01 and EQ-P2-L4-HT02 without loading the downstream cell. Inspect trial parts for dimensional and metallurgical indicators per in-process inspection criteria.
    - Record trial results and decisions to approve or reject production start in the Startup Checklist.

15. Step 9 — Transition to production
    - When trial part results are acceptable and all logs are complete, the shift lead signs the Startup Checklist to authorize production.
    - Notify downstream stations that the line is in production-ready status and reference SOP-P2-L4-02 for any required changeover steps.

Examples and common failure modes
16. Example: If EQ-P2-L4-HP03 shows hydraulic reservoir foaming on first run, verify the correct lubricant CFW-LUB-450 was used and that reservoir vents are unobstructed. Document findings and tag the machine until resolved.
17. Example: If EQ-P2-L4-RR01 produces uneven rolls, confirm CFW-LUB-723 was applied at the correct greasing points and review alignment per Step 6.

Records to keep
18. Maintain the following records in the document control system and equipment binder:
    - Startup Checklist with signatures.
    - Lubricant MRO tickets showing CFW-LUB-450 and CFW-LUB-723 usage.
    - Trial part inspection reports.
    - Any maintenance work orders generated during startup.
    - Reference ECN-2026-045 and SB-1007 entries used during verification.

Training and competency
19. Only personnel trained on Heat Treat line startup and with documented competency per plant training records shall perform these steps. Review training records if unfamiliarity is observed.

Deviations
20. Any deviation from this SOP requires written approval from the P2 maintenance supervisor and must reference ECN-2026-045 for engineering authorizations.

Sign-off
21. Completion of startup is confirmed by signatures below. Signatures must include printed name, role, and time in the Startup Checklist.
    - Operator (print and sign)
    - Maintenance technician (print and sign)
    - Shift lead (print and sign)

References
22. Related documents: ECN-2026-045, SB-1007, SOP-P2-L4-02

Revision history
23. Maintain revision record in the document control header.
